newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Airlines under attack for HK cargo rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Airlines under attack for HK cargo rate rise.

text.p: Airlines flying from Hong Kong to European destinations which have raised official air cargo rates for the second time this year have been criticised for their "short-term opportunism" by the secretary of the Hong Kong Association of Freight Forwarding Agents (HAFFA).
Bengt Sjoeberg, who is also an executive with freight forwarders ASG (HK) Ltd, said the rate rise of up to HK$1.50 per kilo from March 1 was "very unfortunate and shortsighted."

Airlines also raised their ex-Hong Kong market rates by HK$1 a kilo on January 1 as a substitute for a controversial fuel surcharge which was hastily withdrawn by most airlines after protests from shippers and freight forwarders. Many airlines, citing poor yields, also raised their ex-Hong Kong cargo rates twice in the last quarter of last year.

"I don't sympathise at all with this latest rise. They have been too frequent lately and where is the airline's long-term policy? Our clients are getting tired and fed up. It puts forwarders in a very difficult position where many have to absorb the increase because we all know the current peak is only going to last for a short time and rates will come down again. Our rates can't keep on going up and down, we have to stick to a certain policy," HAFFA's Sjoeberg said.
"Airlines putting rates up and down is not beneficial for the market and we would much prefer a much more stable rate policy from carriers than what they have been doing lately," Sjoeberg said.

Industry sources said the carriers were taking advantage of strong demand for space to European destinations from the territory and Hong Kong's de facto flag carrier Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd led the way for the latest rate rise in a further bid to tightly control its home market.
Some rival airlines were not in favour of another rise but quickly followed suit, the sources added.

Hong Kong's all-cargo carrier AHK Air Hong Kong, which is majority owned by Cathay, Dubai-based Emirates and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, are among the carriers to have raised their rate, Reuters research showed.

Lufthansa Cargo, which operates a joint venture with Cathay Pacific on 10 weekly freighter flights to Frankfurt, also raised its ex-Hong Kong cargo rates by HK$1 per kilo from March 1, the airline's managing director for China, Hong Kong and Taiwan, Christian Sedelmaier, told Reuters.

The Hong Kong rise follows rate increases of between seven and 10 per cent at all other Lufthansa Cargo destinations, according to an earlier statement by Lufthansa Cargo chairman Wilhelm Althen. He blamed a price war and a sustained and dramatic fall in cargo rates over recent years. Sedelmaier also said a rise was imperative.
"Rates have been down and we faced a heavy fuel bill last year so we had to recover something," he said.

"Customers are never happy about rate rises but the airline industry cannot survive for long if yields become ever lower and costs rise and rise. I think we have done a great deal to streamline our operation to make it very efficient but there is a point when you can no longer rationalise. Now we have to ask users to contribute more just as other transport operators such as railways and taxi operators raise rates annually. They have a good reason and so do we," Sedelmaier said in an interview. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax+5017
